# Plan 3 — Smart Clean, Uninstaller, Status and the Menu-Bar Extra — Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** RoomForMac's three M2 tools work end to end on the bundled engine:
- **Smart Clean** scans, previews, removes exactly the confirmed items and reports each outcome in plain language.
- **Uninstaller** lists apps and previews each app with every leftover and its size. It quits running apps safely and moves the apps to the Trash.
- **Status** shows live CPU, GPU, memory, disk, network and battery cards with 60-sample sparklines and a health line.
- **Menu-bar extra** shows compact gauges, free space, **Quick Scan** and **Open RoomForMac**.

Every destructive run passes one gate and one recorder seam, and Plan 5's allowance plugs into both.

**Architecture:**
- **Engine:**
  - amend patch 0004 (per-leftover sizes; exit 0 when every requested app is blocked);
  - add patch 0006 (real removed sizes on clean `result` events);
  - ship `engine/status-bin` stubs, so `status-go` never sends a Finder Apple event or a Bluetooth query.
- **MoleEngine:**
  - one `EngineRunControl` on `EngineCommand` (a stop that keeps reading output, plus suspend and resume);
  - `RunDiagnostics` for every run, kept in a rotating `~/Library/Logs/RoomForMac/engine.log`;
  - `RunCompletion`;
  - service protocols (`CleanServicing`, `UninstallServicing`, `StatusServicing`) carrying the fixes the research found.
- **App:**
  - `AppModel` owns the feature models (`SmartCleanModel`, `UninstallerModel`, `StatusMonitor`). They are created once the engine is ready and run nothing before onboarding ends.
  - Views are driven by values.
  - One `DestructiveRunQueue` lease.
  - `RemovalGate`, `RemovalRecorder` and `RunReporter` seams, with unlimited or no-op implementations in this plan.
  - An `AppDelegate` owns the model and the window router, and handles launch, reopen, terminate and URLs.
  - A `MenuBarExtra` scene.

**Tech Stack:** as Plan 2 (Swift 6 on Xcode 27.0, SwiftUI with Liquid Glass, Swift Testing, XCTest for UI tests, XcodeGen, bash 3.2 with bats-core). Added: Swift Charts, IOKit (GPU utilization, power sources), `sysctlbyname`, libproc, `NSRunningApplication`/`NSWorkspace`, UserNotifications and Synchronization (`Mutex`). No Go change and no `cmd/status` patch.

**Spec:** §4.4, §4.6, §5.1, §5.2, §5.4, §5.5, §5.6 (menu-bar and notification switches), §6 (notifications, login launch), §7.2 (the allowance seam only), §10, §11 and §13. These are binding:
- Plan 1, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-25-plan-1-engine.md`;
- Plan 2, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-26-plan-2-app-shell.md`, including its "Execution rulings (as built)" and "Known deferred items".

The research behind this plan (Smart Clean, Uninstaller and Status/menu-bar investigations run against a fake home, plus a completeness critique) is summarised in the Rulings.

**Status:** Done. Executed on the branch `plan3/features` (`92c4fb5`..`872e3aa`: Tasks 1–22 in order, each with its own review, four fix rounds along the way (Tasks 4, 11, 14 ×2, 19), a final whole-branch review by four area reviewers, one fix wave settling all 20 findings (`49ba954`..`5afe314`), and a controller amendment narrowing one of those findings (`872e3aa`)) and merged into `main` by fast-forward. 923 unit tests pass in 109 suites, MoleEngine's package tests pass 194 unit + 16 integration, `bats scripts/tests` is 60/60, and `app_bundle.bats` against a signed Release build is 13/13. The UI smoke tests are built but not run: they need Automation Mode, which is on the owner's manual list. This text was updated afterwards to match what was built. Code blocks show the files as the tasks' briefs wrote them; "As built" notes at the top of each task name its commit range, its fix rounds, and later changes from the final fix wave. "Execution rulings (as built)" (after the Rulings section) lists the decisions taken while executing the plan, and "Known deferred items" what the reviews left open.

The plan starts once Plan 2 merges, on a branch `plan3/features` taken from the merged `main`. Plan 2's execution rulings apply, including the bundle ID `com.roomformac.RoomForMac` and the Finder copy that says Finder is only the Trash fallback.

## Global Constraints

Plan 1's and Plan 2's Global Constraints hold, except where revised below.

**Revisions (already ruled in Plan 2's ledger):**
- **Identity:**
  - bundle ID `com.roomformac.RoomForMac`; the UserDefaults domain is the same;
  - helper identifiers `com.roomformac.RoomForMac.engine.<tool>`;
  - test bundles `com.roomformac.RoomForMac.tests` and `com.roomformac.RoomForMac.uitests`;
  - `CFBundleURLName` `com.roomformac.RoomForMac`, URL scheme `roomformac`.
  - Any Plan 2 text naming `com.roomformac.app` is superseded.
- **`NSAppleEventsUsageDescription`** is the ledger's revised string: Finder is only the Trash fallback. No Plan 3 code, and no engine command Plan 3 starts, sends Finder an Apple event.
- **Engine layout** adds `Contents/Resources/engine/status-bin/{osascript,system_profiler}`. These are scripts, so they stay in Resources.

**Additions:**
- **Engine gate:** no engine command starts before `AppModel.isOnboarded` is true and `AppModel.engine` is `.ready` (Plan 2 Ruling 10). Feature models exist once the engine is ready, and refuse to start engine commands until onboarding completes.
- **Engine patches follow Plan 1's workflow:**
  1. Edit only in `build/mole-work` (`scripts/mole-patches.sh start`) and commit there.
  2. Run `scripts/mole-patches.sh export`, then `scripts/build-engine.sh`.
  3. Run the patch's bats files with `scripts/mole-patches.sh test`, then Mole's full suite. The three upstream failures listed in Plan 1's Environment notes are known.

  Rules for the patched code:
  - bash 3.2, `set -euo pipefail`, `shfmt -i 4 -ci -sr`, `shellcheck`;
  - inert unless a host variable is set;
  - in bats, a `[[ ]]` that is not the last statement ends with `|| return 1`.

  Agents cannot use interactive git flags, so an amendment is `git commit --fixup=<sha>` followed by `git rebase --autosquash <pinned commit>`, which is non-interactive from git 2.44 on (this Mac has 2.54).
- **One engine build at a time** (Plan 2): `build-engine.sh` and `bats scripts/tests` both re-clone `build/engine-src`.
- **MoleEngine:**
  - `swift-tools-version: 6.2`, no dependencies, unit tests in Swift Testing.
  - The `Engine integration` suite runs with `RFM_ENGINE_DIR=$PWD/build/engine`, only against `FakeHome`: never the real home, the real Trash or real caches.
  - Tests start `status-go` only through `StatusService`, with the stubs on `PATH` and a fake `HOME`.
- **App unit tests use fakes only** (Ruling 25). They never start `MoleRunner`, IOKit, `sysctl`, `NSRunningApplication.terminate`, `UNUserNotificationCenter` or `SMAppService`.
- **Destructive runs happen only when all of these hold:**
  - they hold the `DestructiveRunQueue` lease;
  - `RemovalGate` answered `.allow`;
  - they touch only items or apps the user confirmed in a preview.

  `RemovalRecorder` receives each confirmation as it arrives, not at the end of the run.
- **Privacy:** these carry no path, file name or app name: `RemovalConfirmation`, `ScanReport`, `CleanupReport`, notification text, and anything Plan 5 may send. Paths exist only in memory, in the engine's scratch files, in `~/Library/Logs/RoomForMac`, and in diagnostics the user copies.
- **Copy:**
  - Engine strings are mapped to String Catalog copy: section names, `result.detail`, `app_result.reason`, `health_score_msg`.
  - An unmapped value appears only as data ("The cleaner reported: …") or in **Show details**.
  - `app_result.reason` is never used as a title, because some reasons say "Mole" (trademark rule).
- **Units:**
  - The engine reports KiB; Swift works in bytes (KiB × 1024).
  - Sizes are shown with `ByteText`: `ByteCountFormatStyle(style: .file)`, decimal like Finder. Rates are MiB/s (binary).
  - Hero numerals use `Typography.hero`; sizes use `Typography.numeral` in `Palette.grass`.
- **Motion and accessibility:**
  - Plan 2's rules apply.
  - Sparklines never animate data changes.
  - The Scan button morphs through `morphingGlass` and `Motion.glassTransition(reduceMotion:)`.
  - Every interactive element has an `AccessibilityID`, and every card has one combined VoiceOver label.
- **Energy:**
  - At most one `status-go` process per app run, suspended as Ruling 16 describes.
  - No timers run without a demand; the free-space timer runs only while the extra is in the menu bar.
- **Hygiene (Plan 2 ledger):**
  - DerivedData lives at `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/RoomForMac-plan3`.
  - A test that could raise a TCC prompt runs only with `RFM_ALLOW_PROMPTS=1`.
  - UI tests are built but not run, because they need Automation Mode; running them goes on the owner's list.
  - A test must be able to fail. Render tests compare pixels with Plan 2's `RenderedPixels`: the image differs from an empty frame, and light differs from dark.
- **Commits:** conventional subjects. Every commit ends with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.

## Rulings (decisions this plan takes on the owner's behalf)

1. **Amend patch 0004 in place: `leftover_items` on `app` events, and exit 0 when every requested app is blocked** (uninstaller research §5–6, option A).
   - Both changes correct 0004's own contract: its per-app size promise (spec §4.3 P3), and the protocol's rule that a run with only `app_blocked` events exits 0.
   - The per-leftover sizes reuse the engine's one existing measurement, so the drawer's rows add up to the header total.
   - A per-path size timeout becomes `size_known:false` instead of zeroing the total.
   - `leftovers: [String]` stays for compatibility.

   *If wrong:* if the owner wants a separate patch 0007, that is a mechanical split with no interface change. If the owner declines sizes, every row reads `LeftoverSize.unknown`.
2. **New patch 0006 reports removed sizes on clean `result` events.**
   - A `removed` result carries `size_kb` whenever the engine measured the item (0 is a valid size). It is absent only when measuring failed.
   - Measuring happens whenever `MOLE_JSON_EVENTS_FILE` is set, even with `MO_NO_OPLOG=1`.
   - `skipped` and `failed` results never carry it.
   - The charged bytes, the "Freed" figure and Plan 5's ledger all use it (spec §7.2; critique B2/G-d).

   *If wrong (patch declined):* parse the decimal `detail`, which is off by up to ±0.05 MB, behind the same `ItemResult.sizeBytes`.
3. **`status-go` runs with `engine/status-bin` first on its `PATH`.**
   - `osascript` always exits 1 (the ledger's Finder ruling).
   - `system_profiler` refuses `SPBluetoothDataType` and runs `/usr/sbin/system_profiler` for everything else. This closes the unverified Bluetooth prompt (U6) without a patch.
   - Both are required, executable files of `EngineInstallation`, so the launch check catches a bundle that lacks them. Only `StatusService` uses them.

   *If wrong:* Status loses Finder's purgeable-aware free space, which the app reads itself anyway (Ruling 16). Dropping the wrapper is one script line.
4. **One `EngineRunControl` replaces the research's `EngineStop` and `EngineProcessControl`** (critique C11).
   - It is a property of `EngineCommand`, so `EngineRunning` does not change and existing fakes still compile.
   - `stop()` keeps reading: every line written before the process exits is delivered, then the stream throws `EngineError.cancelled`. This fixes G1: today a `removed` result written after the stop is dropped.
   - `suspend()` and `resume()` send SIGSTOP and SIGCONT to the process group.
   - Every stop, Task cancellation included, sends SIGTERM and then SIGCONT, so a suspended group ends at once instead of after the 5 s grace period.
   - Task cancellation stays a hard abort, as today.

   *If wrong:* a second control type later; each caller changes one argument.
5. **Every run keeps diagnostics, and no path leaves the Mac.**
   - Each run produces one `RunDiagnostics`, just before its stream ends: the command, times, how it exited, event counts, and the last ≤ 64 KiB of stdout and of stderr.
   - An events-file run's stdout goes to `EngineCommand.stdoutLog` instead of `/dev/null`.
   - The features append each record to `~/Library/Logs/RoomForMac/engine.log` through `EngineLogStore`: 1 MiB × 5 files, the folder 0700, the files 0600.
   - **Show details** and **Copy diagnostics** read that log.
   - `MO_NO_OPLOG` stays unset, and the engine's own `~/Library/Logs/mole` is left alone.

   *If wrong:* change the tail size, one constant.
6. **Only `RunCompletion.classify(summary:error:stopRequested:)` decides how a run ended.**
   - Services throw only `EngineError`; a `RunFiles` failure becomes `.launchFailed`.
   - A summary with exit 0 wins over a stop that raced it, because the run finished.

   *If wrong:* one more case, and a switch to update in each of two models.
7. **Fresh sizes:** a plan uses the sizes of the latest scan (spec §7.2).
   - `CleanService.rescan` and `CleanSelection.refresh` ship.
   - They run automatically only when **Clean** is pressed on a preview older than 15 minutes (phase `.refreshing`, which can be stopped). Items that vanished drop out; items that grew show their new size.
   - Patch 0006 makes the charged bytes real either way.

   *If wrong:* a stale preview costs one scan-length wait; `freshnessLimit = .infinity` turns the check off.
8. **Removal seams for Plan 5** (critique C9 and B1).
   - `RemovalGate.check` runs before any side effect:
     - Smart Clean calls it in `requestClean()`, before the confirmation sheet;
     - the Uninstaller calls it in `confirm()`, before any app is asked to quit.
   - `RemovalRecorder.record` receives a path-free `RemovalConfirmation {feature, run, sequence, bytes}` as each removal is confirmed (spec §10).
   - `(run, sequence)` is Plan 5's idempotency key, which settles the ledger-schema conflict.
   - Plan 3 ships `UnlimitedRemovalGate` and `NoOpRemovalRecorder`, and writes no ledger.

   *If wrong:* Plan 5 changes one protocol and two call sites.
9. **Charged bytes:**
   - Smart Clean charges `ItemResult.sizeBytes`, or the previewed size when it is missing, once per confirmed path.
   - The Uninstaller charges `freed_kb` for each removed app. It already leaves out leftovers that stayed in place, and a move to the Trash counts (spec §10).

   *If wrong:* one function per feature.
10. **Unknown-size items are selectable and selected by default**, as in Mole. They are tagged "Size unknown", and totals read "at least 4.2 GB".
    - `RemovalRequest.hasUnknownSizes` lets Plan 5 restrict them for unlicensed users.
    - With patch 0006 they are charged the size measured at deletion. Only an item the engine cannot measure even then is charged its preview size of 0.

    *If wrong:* deselecting them by default is one line in `CleanPreview`.
11. **Never offered in M2:**
    - **Smart Clean:** items in the "Time Machine" section, whose real run can only fail, and items whose parent folder the user cannot write. Both are tagged "Needs your password", cannot be selected, and are never sent.
    - **Uninstaller:** Homebrew casks and `needs_sudo` apps (before a preview: casks, or apps whose parent folder is not writable). They are disabled and never sent, because a single one aborts the engine's whole batch with nothing removed.

    Standard (non-admin) users therefore see every `/Applications` app as needing a password until Plan 7. *If wrong:* Plan 7 flips `allowsAdministrator`.
12. **One app-wide `DestructiveRunQueue` — a lease, not a waiting line** (critique Q10).
    - A Smart Clean clean and an Uninstaller removal each hold the lease for the whole run. Terrain and Plan 7 join later.
    - A second request is refused, and its button reads "Wait for <the other> to finish". Nothing destructive ever starts later, when the user may not be watching.
    - Scans, rescans, lists and previews are not destructive and never take the lease.
    - Quitting while the lease is held ends the app only after the run:
      - during a Smart Clean run the dialog offers **Stop and Quit**;
      - during an uninstall it offers **Quit When Done**, because an uninstall cannot be stopped midway.

    *If wrong:* a first-in-first-out queue later, behind the same lease API.
13. **RoomForMac's own data is never cleanable** (critique Q9).
    - `ProtectedPaths.roomForMac` lists `~/Library/Application Support/RoomForMac` and `~/Library/Logs/RoomForMac`.
    - It also lists, for the bundle ID, `~/Library/Caches/<id>`, `~/Library/HTTPStorages/<id>` and `<id>.binarycookies`, `~/Library/WebKit/<id>`, `~/Library/Preferences/<id>.plist` and `~/Library/Saved Application State/<id>.savedState`.
    - It also lists `~/.roomformac` and the running bundle.
    - `CleanService` enforces the list itself:
      - preview rows equal to, inside or containing a protected path are dropped;
      - selections never pass such paths to the engine.
    - An integration test on a fake home pins it. The Uninstaller hides the running bundle.

    *If wrong:* a regenerable cache is kept, and nothing else changes.
14. **Quitting apps before an uninstall** (uninstaller research §9) happens only after the gate allows. The steps:
    1. `terminate()` the app's main instances, then any nested helpers still running. App extensions (`.appex`) and RoomForMac's own process are never touched.
    2. Wait up to 10 s.
    3. Ask separately before **Force Quit**, then wait up to 5 s.
    4. Hold back apps still running and report them "Still open".

    The engine's `pkill -x <executable>` would also kill an unrelated process with the same executable name, so an app whose executable name matches another running process is held back with "Another open app has the same name". No patch is needed for that.

    When an app cannot be moved to the Trash (`trashAccessDenied`), the summary offers `SystemSettingsLink.appManagement`.

    *If wrong:* manual checks U3 and U4 decide whether onboarding needs another card.
15. **Uninstaller list and summary:**
    - `listApps(measureColdSizes: true)` sets `MOLE_UNINSTALL_INLINE_DU_MAX_COLD_ROWS=100000`, with no patch. With it, a cold list had sizes for all 40 apps.
    - Each session re-lists once in the background 30 s after the first list, to pick up the engine's refreshed last-used dates.
    - Leftovers are listed with their sizes but cannot be deselected one by one (roadmap decision 1).
    - "Empty Trash" stays a hint with **Open Trash**, because emptying is irreversible and needs Finder Automation.
    - A removal cannot be cancelled once it starts.
    - The engine's `sensitive_data` flag is not shown: it is true for almost every app.

    *If wrong:* each point is local to the Uninstaller.
16. **Status runs one `status-go --watch --interval 2s` per app run**, shared by the window and the menu bar, and paused and resumed as demand changes:
    - **live** while the Status section is on screen or the menu-bar panel is open;
    - **background** is reserved and unused in M2 (controller ruling, 2026-09-27): with only the menu-bar extra shown and its panel closed, the cadence is **paused**, because the label shows no live numbers and a resumed process delivers a reading within about 0.5 s of the panel opening. This saves about 3% of a core all day;
    - **paused** otherwise; after 5 minutes paused, the process ends.

    Timing: a faster cadence applies at once. A slower one waits 15 s before dropping to background, and 30 s before pausing. History is a 60-sample ring.

    The app reads these itself, because the engine's values are empty or wrong on macOS 27:
    - GPU use, from IOKit `IOAccelerator`;
    - memory pressure, from `kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level`;
    - free space, from `volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsage`, off the main actor: every 60 s while the extra is shown, when the panel opens, and after every run;
    - whether there is a battery, from `IOPSCopyPowerSourcesInfo`.

    Health appears only after the first full (enriched) snapshot, and the engine's English message is parsed into enums.

    *If wrong:* restarting the process for each cadence needs no engine change. Re-enabling background polling (spec §4.4's literal "10 s when only the menu bar is open") is one line in `StatusCadence.resolve`: `menuBarInserted` → `.background`.
17. **Menu-bar extra:**
    - `MenuBarExtra(isInserted:)` is bound through a setter that writes only when the value changes. Apple's documented `@AppStorage` binding made SwiftUI loop, with more than 21,000 body evaluations in 30 s.
    - `menuBarInserted` is `menuBarEnabled && isOnboarded && engine == .ready`.
    - The `menuBar.enabled` preference defaults to **on**.
    - Settings → General gets the switch, replacing Plan 2's note.
    - The label is a static template symbol, with no live numbers.
    - The Dock icon stays `.regular`.

    *If wrong:* the default is one constant.
18. **Window lifecycle:**
    - Closing the last window does not quit while the extra is shown.
    - When the extra was on and onboarding was done at launch, the `Window` uses `.defaultLaunchBehavior(.suppressed)` and `.restorationBehavior(.disabled)`. `AppDelegate` then opens it, unless this is a login launch (`keyAELaunchedAsLogInItem`).
    - A Dock click with no window open reopens it through `WindowRouter`.
    - `AppDelegate` owns `AppModel` and `WindowRouter`, and starts the engine check in `applicationDidFinishLaunching`. Without that, a suppressed window would never run `start()`, and the extra would never appear.

    *If wrong:* if macOS never flags login launches (U5), the window shows at login, which is harmless.
19. **Deep-link hook for Plan 5** (critique U7):
    - `AppDelegate.application(_:open:)` passes each URL to `DeepLink.parse`, then to `AppModel.receive`, which stores it in `pendingDeepLink`; the window is shown.
    - Plan 3 recognises only `roomformac://purchased?checkout_id=<[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}>`. Everything else is ignored, and no URL ever carries a license key.
    - `Window` declares `.handlesExternalEvents(matching: [])`.
    - Plan 5 consumes the link with `takeDeepLink()`.

    *If wrong:* U7 fails in one app state; add an `onOpenURL` fallback.
20. **Notifications** (critique Q6). One is posted only when all hold:
    - `notificationsWanted` is on;
    - the Notifications permission is `.granted`;
    - RoomForMac is not the active app.

    Triggers:
    - a Smart Clean scan finished;
    - a Smart Clean cleanup ended, however it ended;
    - an uninstall ended.

    Text contains counts and sizes only, never a name. Clicking a notification opens the matching section. There are no low-space or scheduled notifications in v1.

    Settings → General gets "Notify me when a scan or cleanup finishes", so `notificationsWanted` gains a second writer (this revises Plan 2 Task 14).

    *If wrong:* the triggers live in two pure functions.
21. **Scan progress:**
    - It shows elapsed time and the current section, never an estimated time left.
    - The progress ring is weighted by the previous scan's time per section, stored locally in `clean.sectionTimings` (never sent), or a built-in table.
    - `CleanSections` in MoleEngine lists the engine's section names; an integration test pins them. Titles are localized in the app, and an unknown name shows as data.

    *If wrong:* cosmetic.
22. **`RunReporter` seam:** features report path-free `ScanReport` and `CleanupReport` values through one composite reporter. It currently feeds the notifier and the Status free-space refresh; Plan 5's telemetry plugs into it later. *If wrong:* one extra layer of indirection.
23. **No recovery of orphaned runs in Plan 3** (Smart Clean research G7).
    - If the app crashes while cleaning, the engine finishes the confirmed selection unattended, and those bytes are not charged. That favours the user.
    - Plan 5 adds the run journal together with the ledger.

    *If wrong:* it becomes Plan 5 scope.
24. **The placeholders go away.** Plan 2's `SectionPlaceholderView`, its three placeholder views and `AccessibilityID.placeholder(_:)` are deleted. Their tests move to the features' identifiers (Tasks 12, 15, 18, 21). *If wrong:* none.
25. **Test isolation:**
    - `AppDependencies`'s defaults are inert: `EngineServices.unavailable`, `StatusSensors.unavailable`, `RunningApps.none`, a log store with no folder, and no notification poster.
    - Only `live()` connects real ones.
    - DEBUG UI-test scenarios get scripted services.

    *If wrong:* none.

## Execution rulings (as built)

Decisions the controller took while executing this plan, from the execution ledger (`.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-27-plan-3-features/progress.md`), in the order they were taken. Each lists what it costs if wrong.

**Preflight scan** (before Task 1, applied while replaying the plan against `main` at `92c4fb5`):

- **PS1.** Status cadence, with only the menu-bar extra shown, is paused rather than polling every 10 s in the background (revises skeleton Ruling 16). The label shows no live numbers, and a resumed `status-go` answers within about 0.5 s of the panel opening; this saves about 3% of a core all day. *If wrong:* one line in `StatusCadence.resolve` re-enables background polling (spec §4.4 literally says 10 s); recorded as a spec erratum in Task 22. (Revised again by the final review — see FW2 below.)
- **PS2.** `RemovalGateNotice` is feature-aware (`RemovalGateNotice(decision:feature:)`, defaulting to `.smartClean`; identifiers `smartClean.gateNotice`/`uninstaller.gateNotice`), so the Uninstaller reuses Smart Clean's copy and identifier instead of writing its own. *If wrong:* none — invisible in M2, since the gate always allows.
- **PS3.** Quitting stops Smart Clean's and the Uninstaller's read-only engine runs (scan/refresh, list/preview) in `applicationWillTerminate`, after the Status monitor stops; otherwise they keep running, unattended, as orphaned process groups. *If wrong:* a run that would have finished harmlessly is cut short at quit.
- **PS4.** Task 2's Interface issue — items sized by `safe_clean`'s own step arrive with `size_kb` 0 when that measurement fails — is left as documented, not patched: about 20 call sites share the pattern, and the gap under-charges, which favours the user. *If wrong:* a few unmeasurable items are charged 0 bytes against Plan 5's allowance.
- **PS5.** The menu-bar item also shows while the launch's engine check is still running or has failed (`AppModel.menuBarItemShown`, Task 19); otherwise a suppressed-window login launch with a broken engine would show nothing at all. *If wrong:* a menu-bar item that only ever says "Starting…" or "needs to be reinstalled".
- **PS6.** Implementers ran on Sonnet 5, and task reviewers on Sonnet 5 except Tasks 4, 11, 14, 17 and 19 (runner/state-machine/lifecycle concurrency), which ran on Opus, as did fix rounds 4 and 5 — the plan text already contains complete code, and Opus session limits were hit four times during authoring. *If wrong:* more fix rounds.

**During execution:**

- **X1** (Task 1, standing for every later task). Subagent commits carry the Co-Authored-By trailer of the model that actually wrote them (Claude Sonnet 5), per the harness's attribution instruction to that agent, not the brief's or `environment.md`'s literal "Claude Opus 5.5" line. Every task report flags this as its one procedural deviation from the brief. *If wrong:* cosmetic trailer text only.
- **X2** (Task 4, fix round 1). `EngineRunControl.detach` takes the `ProcessControl` it is detaching and only clears the phase when it is still that process, instead of unconditionally; a regression test reuses one control across two runs and proves the stop still reaches the second. The brief explicitly allows reusing a control. *If wrong:* none.
- **X3** (Task 11, fix round 1). Three Task 11 minors were promoted into one fix round: `requestClean()` re-checks the phase after the recheck returns (a Clean press must never silently do nothing); `isFresh` treats a preview dated in the future as stale (Ruling 7, under a clock change); `gateDecision` is cleared on any transition outside `.results`. Each is a small correctness gap in a state machine later tasks build on. *If wrong:* one fix round (already spent).
- **X4** (Task 14, fix rounds 1–2). Two Task 14 minors were promoted into fix round 1: `remove()` re-checks same-name clashes immediately before calling `uninstall` and holds back any new clash (Review Focus 3: the engine's `pkill -x` must never hit an unrelated process); a helper asked for the first time in the poll's final round gets one more `pollInterval` before being reported a survivor. The re-review found the second fix incomplete — the grace was a single value fixed by the first app's helper, so a second app's helper asked at the deadline could still get ~0 s — and fix round 2 made it extend per newly-asked helper, bounded by the helper count. *If wrong:* one more fix round (already spent).
- **X5** (Task 19, fix round 1). Before `AppDelegate.terminationReply()` returns `.terminateLater`, it brings the main window forward on the section holding the lease (`.uninstaller` for `waitForUninstall`, `.smartClean` for `stopCleaning`) via `router.showMain(section:)`; a test pins `router.pending`. A quit must never wait on a question the user cannot see. *If wrong:* the window pops up during a quit that would otherwise finish unattended.

**Final whole-branch review** (four area reviewers; one fix wave `49ba954..5afe314`, then a controller amendment `872e3aa`):

- **FW1.** One final fix wave covers 20 of the review's 24 findings (all but 4 minors): each is small, several are user-visible copy or accessibility errors, and three are safety issues (self-uninstall through a symlink, pkill name matching, dead `protectedPaths` wiring). *If wrong:* a larger single fix diff for the same total amount of work.
- **FW2.** Revises PS1/Ruling 16: the free-space timer runs only while Status is live — the section on screen or the menu-bar panel open — not merely while the menu-bar icon shows. Nothing displays the value while only the icon shows, and the disk card needs a fresh read once the section (or panel) does. *If wrong:* the menu-bar panel shows free space as of its last open until it refreshes on appear, which it still does.
- **FW3.** Revises the final wave's own pkill ruling (F2 in `final-fix-report.md`): an app whose executable name contains regex metacharacters is held back only when another running process actually matches it the way `pkill -x` would (the full `argv[0]` name, as a regex), not unconditionally — "always" made apps such as Zoom (`zoom.us`) impossible to uninstall from RoomForMac. *If wrong:* an exotic pattern could still reach an unrelated process if the matcher misses a case. (Commit `872e3aa`, after the final wave; see Tasks 13–15's As-built notes.)
- **FW4.** The live `RunningApps` test reads its own process's `argv[0]` with a read-only `sysctl(KERN_PROCARGS2)` call: read-only, and only about this process. The Global Constraints' "no sysctl readers in tests" rule targets the Status sensors, not this. *If wrong:* none.
- **FW5.** F17 (dead `protectedPaths`) was resolved by deleting the unused `AppDependencies.protectedPaths` — the live services already build `ProtectedPaths.live()` themselves — and pinning, with a test, that the live clean service actually carries RoomForMac's own paths. *If wrong:* none.

- **Engine (Mole patches):** `_batch_measure_leftovers` is O(n²) in the leftover count (Task 1, brief-prescribed; lists stay small).

- **MoleEngine — Clean/Uninstall/Status services:** no `ProtectedPaths` regression guard for `/`, and `docs/engine-protocol.md`'s Smart Clean host notes partly repeat the Clean events section (Task 6). `rootDiskPrefersTheStartupVolume` uses `try #require(SystemSnapshot.decode(...))` on a call that cannot throw — four compiler notes, left as the brief mandated (Task 8).
- **Uninstaller — running-app matching (parked from the final review):** `PkillPattern` matches in the C locale while the engine's own `pkill` runs under `en_US.UTF-8`; a `.`/bracket pattern that happens to line up with a non-ASCII character in another process's name could be missed. Fix later with `regcomp_l`/`regexec_l` under a UTF-8 locale (count a match in either). *Cost if wrong:* an unrelated process with an unusual non-ASCII name could be ended by an uninstall. `liveProcesses()` reads `argv[0]` (a 1 MiB buffer, `KERN_PROCARGS2`) for every process on the Mac, per removable app, on the main actor — 11–25 ms per enumeration, about 0.5 s for 20 apps; acceptable for M2, enumerate once per `holdBackNameClashes` call later. *Cost if wrong:* a brief stall when confirming a large uninstall.
- **Uninstaller — model and list:** Step 10's RED was not independently observed (session stalls; mutation checks substitute instead — see Task 13's As-built note); `FailureReason.other` suppresses any explanation containing "mole" as a substring, even inside another word (Task 13, brief-mandated). A stale-preview regression test busy-waits with `Task.yield()`, bounded only by the suite's one-minute time limit (Task 14, brief-mandated). `AppListView` computes "last used" against `Date()` directly in the view body, not through an injectable clock; the `forceQuitRequest` binding's setter may call `cancel()` twice on one Escape press, which is idempotent (Task 15).

The live item labeler asks Launch Services on the main actor once per row while building a preview — memoize by bundle ID later; coverage gaps in a recheck completing despite a Stop, fallback diagnostics for `unexpectedRemovals`, a stale gate answer surviving a selection change, no double-click guard, and the clean-ending order (log → reporter → lease end) untested directly (Task 11). `heroRendersWithAndWithoutFullDiskAccess` varies Full Disk Access, `blockedBy` and the note together, so its pixel difference is not isolated to the Full Disk Access card alone (Task 12). A lost background re-list if it fires while quitting or removing, and the zero-removed stop headline "Cleaning stopped before anything was removed." can sit next to `.interrupted` rows that say part of an item may be gone — parked, deferred to the next Smart Clean touch: drop the claim when any outcome is `.interrupted` (final review). *Cost if wrong:* a confusing summary after a Stop that lands mid-deletion, which is rare.

## Review Focus

1. **A stop, quit or crash in the middle of a destructive run.**
   - Expected:
     - every late result arrives;
     - every plan item gets exactly one outcome;
     - each removal is recorded once;
     - no engine is left running after a normal quit.
   - Pinned by:
     - Task 4 (a late line, then `.cancelled`);
     - Task 11 ("stop during cleaning" and "confirmation once per path");
     - Task 19 (`TerminationDecision` and the terminate-later flow).
2. **The disk changes between preview and run.**
   - Examples:
     - an item vanished or grew;
     - a covered child was selected alone;
     - the engine reports `skipped` for paths the user did not select;
     - an app changed or is blocked on rescan;
     - some leftovers fail to move.
   - Expected: accurate outcomes and charges.
   - Pinned by: Task 6 (tally and `refresh`), Task 7 (preview fixes and tally), and Tasks 10 and 13 (deriving outcomes and summaries).
3. **Things that must never be touched or charged:**
   - RoomForMac's own data;
   - Time Machine and other admin items;
   - apps that need a password, one of which aborts the whole batch;
   - apps quit before the gate allowed it (B1);
   - unrelated processes with the same executable name.
   - Pinned by:
     - Task 6's protected-paths integration test and Task 9's guard;
     - Task 10 (access rules);
     - Task 14 ("a gate refusal never terminates an app" and "password apps are never sent");
     - Task 13 (name clashes).
4. **The Status process under changing demand.**
   - Expected:
     - exactly one `status-go`;
     - SIGCONT follows SIGTERM;
     - no Finder or Bluetooth use;
     - first-snapshot artifacts are handled (not yet enriched, zero rates);
     - `collected_at` parses in all five forms.
   - Pinned by:
     - Task 4 (cancelled while suspended ends in under 1 s);
     - Task 8 (date forms and the stub `PATH`);
     - Task 17 (`feedOpenCount == 1` and the grace periods).
5. **The menu-bar extra and the window lifecycle:**
   - the `isInserted` loop;
   - closing the last window;
   - login launches;
   - Dock reopen;
   - deep links when the window is closed, when the app is menu-bar only, and when it is not running;
   - Quick Scan while a clean runs.
   - Pinned by: Task 19 (the binding write count, `AppDelegate` and `WindowRouter` tests); U5 and U7 are manual checks.

## Tasks

The task text below is the requirements contract. The **Interfaces** blocks are binding: names, types and signatures must match across tasks exactly. Plan 2's names are consumed as Plan 2 declares them.

### Task 1: Engine — amend patch 0004 (leftover items, exit 0 when everything is blocked)

**As built** (`92c4fb5..5ff3c0d`: `5ff3c0d`; review clean). Built as written. Patch 0005 was re-exported with only its context line numbers shifted (no functional change).

**Files:**
- Modify (Mole, in `build/mole-work`):
  - `lib/uninstall/batch.sh`: a new `_batch_measure_leftovers`; the leftover sizing in `_batch_scan_app_details`; the host-mode exit status in `batch_uninstall_applications`.
  - `lib/core/host.sh`: an optional 11th argument to `mole_json_event_app`, and a new `mole_json_leftover_items`.
  - `tests/uninstall_host_mode.bats`: new cases.
- Modify (RoomForMac):
  - `patches/mole/0004-Add-a-host-driven-uninstall-mode.patch` (rewritten);
  - `patches/mole/0005-*.patch` (re-exported);
  - `docs/engine-protocol.md` (Uninstall section).

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes:
  - Plan 1 patch 0004: `mole_json_event_app` (10 arguments), `mole_json_array_from_lines`, `uninstall_host_paths_mode`, `MOLE_UNINSTALL_APP_PATHS_FILE`, `MOLE_UNINSTALL_PREVIEW_ONLY`, `MOLE_ASSUME_YES`;
  - `scripts/mole-patches.sh start|export|test|lint`.
- Produces:
  - **Wire format:**
    - Each `app` event gains `"leftover_items":[{"path":"…","size_kb":N,"size_known":true|false,"covered_by":"…"|null},…]`, in the same order as `leftovers`.
    - A covered row has `size_kb:0`, and `covered_by` names the nearest listed ancestor.
    - The app's `size_kb` keeps its meaning: the bundle plus the uncovered leftovers whose size is known.
    - With `MOLE_UNINSTALL_APP_PATHS_FILE` set, a run where every requested app ended as `app_blocked` exits **0**, in previews and real runs alike.
  - **Bash:**
    - `_batch_measure_leftovers FILES` prints `size_kb\037known\037covered_by\037path` lines. `\037` is the unit separator; a tab would collapse an empty field.
    - `mole_json_event_app`'s optional 11th argument is a pre-rendered JSON array; it defaults to `[]`.
- Internal to this task (no other task consumes them):
  - `_batch_sum_leftover_rows ROWS` (`lib/uninstall/batch.sh`) prints the KiB total of `_batch_measure_leftovers` rows. Covered, missing and unknown rows print 0, so the total is the sum of the uncovered, known sizes.
  - `mole_json_leftover_items ROWS` (`lib/core/host.sh`) turns those rows into the JSON array for the 11th argument; an empty `covered_by` becomes `null`.
  - `tests/uninstall_host_mode.bats`: `run_host_uninstall` sources `OVERRIDES=<file>` (extra engine-function redefinitions) just before `main`; new helpers `create_fixture_with_nested_leftover` and `run_with_uninstall_functions` (runs a script from stdin in a bash that sourced `bin/uninstall.sh` without `main`).

**Requirements:**
- **Workflow:**
  1. Run `scripts/mole-patches.sh start`.
  2. Edit and commit with `git -C build/mole-work commit --fixup=<sha of "Add a host-driven uninstall mode">`.
  3. Run `git -C build/mole-work rebase --autosquash "$(git -C vendor/mole rev-parse HEAD)"`.
  4. Resolve 0005's context in `tests/uninstall_host_mode.bats` if the rebase stops there.
  5. Run `scripts/mole-patches.sh export`, then `scripts/build-engine.sh`.
  6. Check `git diff --stat patches/mole`: only 0004 and 0005 changed.
- **Engine behaviour:**
  - Leftovers are measured once, with the same de-duplication as `calculate_total_size`.
  - A per-path size timeout gives `size_known:false` and 0 for that path only; the total is not zeroed.
  - Paths are JSON-escaped with `mole_json_str`.
  - `leftovers` is unchanged.
- **Exit 0 when everything is blocked** applies only in host-paths mode, and only when there are blocks.
  - A scan failure, a timeout or a signal still exits non-zero.
  - Without host variables the engine behaves exactly like V1.56.0.
- **Bats tests:**
  - A fixture with three leftovers plus one nested leftover gives 4 `leftover_items`. The bundle plus the uncovered known sizes equals `size_kb`. The nested item has `covered_by` set and `size_kb` 0.
  - A forced `du` timeout (`MOLE_TIMEOUT_DISK_VERIFY_SEC=1` with a slow `du` stub) gives `size_known:false`, and the other sizes stay.
  - A path with spaces, quotes and UTF-8 round-trips.
  - Only an official-uninstaller app requested ("Falcon" fixture): the preview **and** the real run exit 0, emit `app_blocked official_uninstaller`, and remove nothing.
  - A missing path plus an official-uninstaller app exits 0.
  - An app in a `chmod 555` `~/Applications` gives `manual_removal` and exit 0.
  - A blocked app plus an app whose scan fails still exits non-zero.
  - Every existing test in `uninstall_host_mode.bats` passes.
- **Checks:** Mole's full suite shows only the three known failures, and `bats scripts/tests` passes.
- **`docs/engine-protocol.md` (Uninstall):**
  - document `leftover_items`;
  - document the all-blocked exit 0;
  - correct `freed_kb`: it is the scanned `size_kb` minus the leftovers that could not be moved, and no event names those leftovers;
  - add the cold-list variable (Ruling 15).

**Decisions this task takes inside the requirements:**
- **Gate.** The new sizing runs only while `MOLE_JSON_EVENTS_FILE` is set; otherwise `_batch_scan_app_details` still calls `calculate_total_size` exactly as V1.56.0 does, zeroing the leftovers' share on a timeout. The exit change is gated on `MOLE_UNINSTALL_APP_PATHS_FILE`. Without host variables nothing differs.
- **One item per `leftovers` line.** `path` and `covered_by` are printed exactly as listed (not trailing-slash-trimmed), so a host matches an item to its `leftovers` entry by string. Beyond the interface:
  - a line that no longer exists is `0`, `size_known:true`, as `calculate_total_size` counts it;
  - a second listing of the same path (for example with a trailing slash) is covered by the first listing;
  - a covered row repeats the `size_known` of the measured row that holds its bytes.
- **At most two timeouts per app.** After two timed-out measurements the app's remaining leftovers are reported `size_known:false` without being measured. Before this patch the first timeout ended the sizing, so a preview waited for at most one 30 s timeout; unbounded per-path timeouts could make an Xcode preview (DerivedData, CoreSimulator, DeviceSupport) wait minutes. A single timeout, which the requirement describes, still affects only its own path.
- **A path containing byte `0x1f`** would break the row format, so it is reported unknown, is never measured and never covers another row. No double counting follows, because an unmeasured row adds nothing.
- **The timeout test uses `MOLE_TIMEOUT_DISK_VERIFY_SEC=2`, not 1.** `get_path_size_kb` turns its budget into a whole-second `SECONDS` deadline and re-reads `SECONDS` a subshell later. With 1, a clock tick in between gives a *fast* path a zero budget and a 124, so the test would flake about once in a hundred runs. With 2 the slow stub still times out (after 1–2 s) and no fast path can.
- **Three end-to-end tests replace discovery through `OVERRIDES`.** They replace `find_app_files`, which gives a deterministic nested leftover and odd path names (discovery never lists a nested pair for a plain fixture). They also replace `uninstall_live_bundle_has_other_install` with "no sibling": an unreadable path in that machine-wide scan (TCC, a slow receipt walk) turns on the sibling guard, which skips leftover discovery entirely. The scan itself (identity checks, blocking, sizing, events, exit status) runs unchanged.

```bash
# Source bin/uninstall.sh (its functions, not main) in a fresh bash, then run
# the script on stdin there. Extra NAME=value arguments become its environment.
run_with_uninstall_functions() {
    local src="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/uninstall_source.sh"
    sourceable_uninstall_sh "$src"
    local script="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/script.sh"
    cat > "$script"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2016  # the inner bash expands these from its environment
    run env HOME="$HOME" PATH="$PATH" SRC_PATH="$src" SCRIPT="$script" MOLE_TEST_NO_AUTH=1 "$@" \
        /bin/bash --noprofile --norc -c 'set -euo pipefail; source "$SRC_PATH"; source "$SCRIPT"'
}
```

Notes on the tests:
- Every `[[ ]]` that is not a test's last statement is part of an `|| skip` list, so the `|| return 1` rule and Mole's `audit_bats_assertions.py` are satisfied. The `[ ]` assertions fail a test wherever they stand.
- The manual-removal test restores the folder's mode right after `run`, before any assertion. `run` never fails, so a later failing assertion cannot leave a 555 folder that would break the next test's `rm -rf` in `setup`.
- The two single-quoted scripts carry the `SC2016` directive that Mole's test lint requires (patch 0005 added the same directive to the older tests).

Replace with:
```bash
# Host mode (MOLE_JSON_EVENTS_FILE): measure each leftover once, for the app
# event's leftover_items. FILES is the newline-separated leftover list that
# the event reports as `leftovers`. Prints one row per non-empty line, in
# order: size_kb, known (true/false), covered_by and path, separated by the
# unit separator (\037; a tab is IFS whitespace and would collapse an empty
# covered_by). path and covered_by are printed as listed, so a host can match
# them to `leftovers`.
#   - De-duplication is calculate_total_size's: a line equal to or inside
#     another existing line is not measured. It prints 0, covered_by names its
#     nearest listed ancestor (or the first listing of the same path), and
#     known repeats the flag of the row whose size holds its bytes.
#   - A missing path prints 0 and true, as calculate_total_size counts it.
#   - A failed or timed-out measurement prints 0 and false for that path only.
#     After two timeouts the remaining paths print 0 and false unmeasured, so
#     one app never waits for more than two size timeouts.
#   - A line containing the separator is never measured (0 and false), and
#     never covers another line.
#   - A signal returns its status, as in calculate_total_size.
# When nothing times out and no line contains the separator, the sizes add
# up to calculate_total_size's total.
_batch_measure_leftovers() {
    local files="${1-}"
    local unit_sep=$'\037'
    local -a raw=() norm=() usable=() known=() sizes=() cover=()
    local line normalized
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -n "$line" ]] || continue
        normalized="${line%/}"
        [[ -n "$normalized" ]] || normalized="$line"
        raw+=("$line")
        norm+=("$normalized")
        sizes+=(0)
        cover+=(-1)
        if [[ "$line" == *"$unit_sep"* ]]; then
            usable+=(false)
            known+=(false)
        elif [[ -e "$line" ]]; then
            usable+=(true)
            known+=(true)
        else
            usable+=(false)
            known+=(true)
        fi
    done <<< "$files"

    local count=${#raw[@]}
    local i j nearest duplicate
    for ((i = 0; i < count; i++)); do
        [[ "${usable[i]}" == true ]] || continue
        nearest=-1
        duplicate=-1
        for ((j = 0; j < count; j++)); do
            if [[ $j -eq $i || "${usable[j]}" != true ]]; then
                continue
            fi
            if [[ "${norm[i]}" == "${norm[j]}" ]]; then
                if [[ $j -lt $i && $duplicate -lt 0 ]]; then
                    duplicate=$j
                fi
            elif [[ "${norm[i]}" == "${norm[j]}"/* ]]; then
                if [[ $nearest -lt 0 ]]; then
                    nearest=$j
                elif [[ ${#norm[j]} -gt ${#norm[nearest]} ]]; then
                    nearest=$j
                fi
            fi
        done
        if [[ $duplicate -ge 0 ]]; then
            cover[i]=$duplicate
        elif [[ $nearest -ge 0 ]]; then
            cover[i]=$nearest
        fi
    done

    local timeouts=0 size_kb size_rc
    for ((i = 0; i < count; i++)); do
        if [[ "${usable[i]}" != true || ${cover[i]} -ge 0 ]]; then
            continue
        fi
        if [[ $timeouts -ge 2 ]]; then
            known[i]=false
            continue
        fi
        size_kb=""
        size_rc=0
        size_kb=$(get_path_size_kb "${norm[i]}") || size_rc=$?
        if mole_rc_timeout "$size_rc"; then
            timeouts=$((timeouts + 1))
            known[i]=false
        elif [[ $size_rc -ge 128 ]]; then
            return "$size_rc"
        elif [[ $size_rc -eq 0 && "$size_kb" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
            sizes[i]=$((10#$size_kb))
        else
            known[i]=false
        fi
    done

    local covered_by target
    for ((i = 0; i < count; i++)); do
        covered_by=""
        if [[ "${usable[i]}" == true && ${cover[i]} -ge 0 ]]; then
            target=${cover[i]}
            covered_by="${raw[target]}"
            while [[ ${cover[target]} -ge 0 ]]; do
                target=${cover[target]}
            done
            known[i]=${known[target]}
        fi
        printf '%s\037%s\037%s\037%s\n' "${sizes[i]}" "${known[i]}" "$covered_by" "${raw[i]}"
    done
}

# Total KiB of _batch_measure_leftovers rows. Covered, missing and unknown
# rows print 0, so this is the sum of the uncovered, known sizes.
_batch_sum_leftover_rows() {
    local rows="${1-}" total=0 row_size
    while IFS=$'\037' read -r row_size _; do
        if [[ "$row_size" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
            total=$((total + 10#$row_size))
        fi
    done <<< "$rows"
    printf '%s\n' "$total"
}

```

How it works:
- The first loop records each line as listed (`raw`) and trimmed of one trailing slash (`norm`), exactly as `calculate_total_size` trims.
- The second loop gives every existing line either a cover (an earlier listing of the same path, else its longest listed ancestor) or none.
- A line with no cover is exactly a member of `calculate_total_size`'s de-duplicated set, and only those lines are measured, once each, on the trimmed path.
- Following `cover` always ends at a measured row: each step goes to a strictly shorter path, or to an earlier listing of the same path. That row's flag is what a covered row repeats.
- Every measured row goes through `get_path_size_kb`, as before, so a folder is still `du -skP` with the same timeout, and a file is still its allocated blocks.
- Errexit is off inside a `$(…) || rc=$?` call, so the function returns only 0 or a signal status and never relies on `set -e`.

### Task 2: Engine — patch 0006, removed sizes on clean results

**As built** (`5ff3c0d..07cc282`: `07cc282`; review clean). Built as written.

**Files:**
- Modify (Mole):
  - `lib/core/host.sh`: an optional 5th argument `size_kb` to `mole_json_event_result`;
  - `lib/core/log.sh`: `log_operation` passes it through;
  - `lib/core/file_ops.sh`: `safe_remove` and `safe_sudo_remove` pass the size they measured, and measure whenever `MOLE_JSON_EVENTS_FILE` is set, even with `MO_NO_OPLOG=1`;
  - any existing assertion in `tests/clean_json_events.bats` or `tests/clean_selection.bats` that matches a whole `removed` line. There is one, in `clean_json_events.bats`, and it needs no change: its `log_operation` call passes four arguments, so its line keeps its shape (Step 8 checks this).
- Create (Mole): `tests/clean_removed_sizes.bats`.
- Modify (RoomForMac):
  - `docs/engine-protocol.md` (Clean events);
  - `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: add `tests/clean_removed_sizes.bats` to "Patch tests".
- Create (RoomForMac): `patches/mole/0006-Report-removed-sizes-in-clean-result-events.patch` (written by `scripts/mole-patches.sh export`, never by hand).

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Task 1's patch queue in `build/mole-work`.
- Produces:
  - On the wire, a `result` with `action:"removed"` may carry `"size_kb":N`, the KiB measured just before removal (0 allowed). The key is absent when the size could not be measured.
  - `skipped` and `failed` never carry it.
  - Dry runs still write no `result` events.
- Bash (internal to this task):
  - `mole_json_event_result COMMAND ACTION PATH DETAIL [SIZE_KB]` appends `,"size_kb":N` after `detail`, and only when `ACTION` is `REMOVED` and `SIZE_KB` is all digits (`mole_json_num` drops leading zeros). Any other `SIZE_KB` leaves the key out.
  - `log_operation COMMAND ACTION PATH [DETAIL] [SIZE_KB]` hands `SIZE_KB` to the event only. The operations-log line keeps its V1.56.0 shape.
  - `safe_remove` and `safe_sudo_remove` keep their signatures. The meaning of their precomputed-size argument is now spelled out: all digits is a measured size and is reported; empty makes the sink measure, as before; anything else counts as unmeasured and is never measured again.

**Interface issue:** "absent when the size could not be measured" holds for every size that `safe_remove` or `safe_sudo_remove` measures itself. Most clean items, though, reach `safe_remove` with a size that `safe_clean`'s own sizing pass (`_safe_clean_impl` in `bin/clean.sh`) measured moments before. When that pass fails, it hands over `0`, and the result then reads `size_kb: 0`. The same pass sizes dry runs, so a preview in which it failed shows the row as `size_kb: 0` with `size_known: true` too. Task 6 needs no change. Its fallback (`outcome.sizeBytes ?? item.sizeBytes`) could only have charged more, and only when the preview's measurement succeeded and the run's failed, so the gap favours the user. Smallest fix, if the owner wants the key left out there too: every section that sizes its own items passes a non-numeric size (for example `unmeasured`) to `safe_remove` or `safe_sudo_remove` for an item it could not measure. `safe_remove` already treats that value as unmeasured after this task. It is not applied here because it is not small: `_safe_clean_impl` alone sizes in three ways (bulk `stat`, parallel subshells whose result files would need a new field, and one at a time), and about twenty other call sites in `lib/clean/*.sh` (`user.sh`, `caches.sh`, `app_caches.sh`, `dev.sh`, `project.sh`, `system.sh`, `apps.sh`) and `lib/core/file_ops.sh` pass their own measured size, which they too leave at 0 after a failed measurement. Fixing only `_safe_clean_impl` would leave the contract uneven.

**Requirements:**
- The patch is standalone, its subject starts "Report removed sizes …", and it is inert without `MOLE_JSON_EVENTS_FILE`.
- The measurement adds no extra `du` when the operations log already measured the item.
- **Bats tests:**
  - A selected real run over a cache that grew after the preview: the `removed` event has `size_kb` ≥ the new size.
  - `MO_NO_OPLOG=1` still gives `size_kb`.
  - A zero-byte file gives `size_kb:0`.
  - An item whose measurement is forced to fail has no `size_kb`.
  - `skipped` and `failed` events have none.
  - A dry run writes no `result`.
- **Checks:** Mole's full suite shows only the known failures, and the CI patch-test list includes the new file.
- **`docs/engine-protocol.md`:**
  - document the new field;
  - note that the `removed` `detail` may be empty and uses decimal units;
  - note that `skipped` results also arrive for paths the host did not select.

**How the size travels:** a section measures its items (for the common `safe_clean` path, `_safe_clean_impl` sizes the whole batch with `get_cleanup_path_size_kb`), then calls `safe_remove PATH true SIZE …`. `safe_remove` uses that size, or measures the path itself with `get_path_size_kb` when no size was passed. Today it does either only while the operations log is on, and it throws the number away once the human-readable `detail` is made. After this task it keeps the number in `size_report_kb`, but only when it is a real measurement, and passes it through `log_operation` to `mole_json_event_result`. That function writes it on `removed` results. Nothing changes without the events file: the gate is `oplog_enabled || mole_json_events_enabled`, and `mole_json_event_result` returns at once when events are off.

- [x] **Step 2: Write the failing tests** — `build/mole-work/tests/clean_removed_sizes.bats`

The pipeline tests reuse `clean_selection.bats`'s seams: mocked toolchains, an `rm` guard that refuses paths outside the fake home, and `run_clean_json` with the host variables RoomForMac sets. The unit tests call `safe_remove` or `safe_sudo_remove` in a fresh shell, with fake `du` or `sudo` where a test needs one. A fake `du` has to be an executable on `PATH` (`mole_test_fake_command`), because `run_with_timeout` execs it and never sees shell functions. `_mole_bounded_sudo` calls a `sudo` shell function when one is defined, so the sudo test defines one.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bats
# Removed sizes on clean result events: a removed result carries the KiB the
# engine measured just before deleting the path, and no other result does.

load helpers/common

setup_file() {
    mole_test_setup_home clean-removed-sizes
}

teardown_file() {
    mole_test_teardown_home
}

setup() {
    if [[ "$HOME" != "${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/tmp-"* ]]; then
        printf 'FATAL: HOME is not a test temp dir: %s\n' "$HOME" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    # A failed test can leave a read-only folder behind.
    chmod -R u+w "$HOME" 2> /dev/null || true
    rm -rf "${HOME:?}"/* "$HOME/.config" "$HOME/.cache" "$HOME/.tmp"
    mkdir -p "$HOME/Library/Caches" "$HOME/.config/mole" "$HOME/.tmp"
    EVENTS="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/events.ndjson"
    SELECTION_FILE=""
    NO_OPLOG=""
    : > "$EVENTS"
}

teardown() {
    chmod -R u+w "$HOME" 2> /dev/null || true
}

# Same seams as clean_selection.bats: no real Homebrew, Xcode, process table
# or open-file probe may influence what the pipeline sees.
set_mock_host_toolchains() {
    MOCK_TOOLCHAIN_BIN="$HOME/toolchain-bin"
    mkdir -p "$MOCK_TOOLCHAIN_BIN"
    cat > "$MOCK_TOOLCHAIN_BIN/brew" << 'MOCK'
#!/bin/bash
case "${1:-}" in
    --cache) echo "$HOME/Library/Caches/Homebrew" ;;
    --prefix) echo "$HOME/homebrew" ;;
esac
exit 0
MOCK
    cat > "$MOCK_TOOLCHAIN_BIN/xcrun" << 'MOCK'
#!/bin/bash
exit 1
MOCK
    cat > "$MOCK_TOOLCHAIN_BIN/lsof" << 'MOCK'
#!/bin/bash
case " $* " in
    *" -p 1 "*) printf 'p1\nu0\n'; exit 0 ;;
    *) exit 1 ;;
esac
MOCK
    cat > "$MOCK_TOOLCHAIN_BIN/ps" << 'MOCK'
#!/bin/bash
printf '  PID  PPID COMM ARGS\n'
MOCK
    chmod +x "$MOCK_TOOLCHAIN_BIN"/*
}

# Test-only guard: any rm aimed outside the fake HOME is refused and logged.
install_rm_guard() {
    RM_GUARD_BIN="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/rm-guard-bin"
    RM_GUARD_LOG="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/rm-refused.log"
    mkdir -p "$RM_GUARD_BIN"
    : > "$RM_GUARD_LOG"
    cat > "$RM_GUARD_BIN/rm" << GUARD
#!/bin/bash
for arg in "\$@"; do
    case "\$arg" in
        -*) ;;
        "$HOME"/*) ;;
        *)
            printf '%s\n' "\$arg" >> "$RM_GUARD_LOG"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
done
exec /bin/rm "\$@"
GUARD
    chmod +x "$RM_GUARD_BIN/rm"
}

# Run bin/clean.sh on the fake home with the host variables RoomForMac sets.
# SELECTION_FILE selects paths; NO_OPLOG=1 turns Mole's operations log off.
run_clean_json() {
    local -a vars=(
        HOME="$HOME" TMPDIR="$HOME/.tmp" MOLE_TEST_MODE=0 MOLE_TEST_NO_AUTH=1 MOLE_NO_AUTH=1
        MOLE_GUI_HOST=roomformac MOLE_LSREGISTER_PATH="" MOLE_JSON_EVENTS_FILE="$EVENTS"
        PATH="$RM_GUARD_BIN:$MOCK_TOOLCHAIN_BIN:$PATH"
    )
    if [[ -n "$SELECTION_FILE" ]]; then
        vars+=(MOLE_SELECTION_FILE="$SELECTION_FILE")
    fi
    if [[ -n "$NO_OPLOG" ]]; then
        vars+=(MO_NO_OPLOG=1)
    fi
    run env "${vars[@]}" "$PROJECT_ROOT/bin/clean.sh" "$@"
}

# A folder holding one KB-sized file of zeros. Args: folder, size in KB.
make_dir_with_blob() {
    mkdir -p "$1"
    dd if=/dev/zero of="$1/blob.bin" bs=1024 count="$2" 2> /dev/null
}

make_cache() {
    make_dir_with_blob "$HOME/Library/Caches/$1" "$2"
}

# Remove TARGET with safe_remove in a fresh shell that sources Mole's core.
# Further VAR=value arguments go into that shell's environment;
# PRECOMPUTED_KB becomes safe_remove's third argument (a caller's own size).
run_safe_remove() {
    local target="$1"
    shift
    run env HOME="$HOME" PROJECT_ROOT="$PROJECT_ROOT" TARGET="$target" "$@" \
        /bin/bash --noprofile --norc << 'EOF'
set -euo pipefail
source "$PROJECT_ROOT/lib/core/common.sh"
safe_remove "$TARGET" true "${PRECOMPUTED_KB-}"
EOF
}

# How many times the recording du double was asked about PATH.
count_du_calls() {
    grep -cF -- "$1" "$HOME/du-calls" || true
}

# The size_kb of the removed result for PATH: "null" when the key is absent,
# nothing when there is no removed result for PATH.
removed_size_of() {
    jq -r --arg p "$1" 'select(.type == "result" and .action == "removed" and .path == $p) | .size_kb' "$EVENTS"
}

@test "result events carry size_kb only on removed results with a measured size" {
    run env HOME="$HOME" EVENTS="$EVENTS" PROJECT_ROOT="$PROJECT_ROOT" MO_NO_OPLOG=1 \
        /bin/bash --noprofile --norc << 'EOF'
set -euo pipefail
source "$PROJECT_ROOT/lib/core/common.sh"
export MOLE_JSON_EVENTS_FILE="$EVENTS"
log_operation "clean" "REMOVED" "/tmp/rfm/a" "1MB" 1024
log_operation "clean" "REMOVED" "/tmp/rfm/zero" "" 0
log_operation "clean" "REMOVED" "/tmp/rfm/padded" "" 007
log_operation "clean" "REMOVED" "/tmp/rfm/symlink" "symlink"
log_operation "clean" "REMOVED" "/tmp/rfm/unmeasured" "" ""
log_operation "clean" "REMOVED" "/tmp/rfm/text" "12KB" "12KB"
log_operation "clean" "SKIPPED" "/tmp/rfm/skipped" "protected" 12
log_operation "clean" "FAILED" "/tmp/rfm/failed" "permission denied" 12
MOLE_DRY_RUN=1 log_operation "clean" "REMOVED" "/tmp/rfm/dry" "" 5
EOF
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    run cat "$EVENTS"
    [ "${#lines[@]}" -eq 8 ]
    [ "${lines[0]}" = '{"v":1,"type":"result","command":"clean","action":"removed","path":"/tmp/rfm/a","detail":"1MB","size_kb":1024}' ]
    [ "${lines[1]}" = '{"v":1,"type":"result","command":"clean","action":"removed","path":"/tmp/rfm/zero","detail":"","size_kb":0}' ]
    [ "${lines[2]}" = '{"v":1,"type":"result","command":"clean","action":"removed","path":"/tmp/rfm/padded","detail":"","size_kb":7}' ]
    [ "${lines[3]}" = '{"v":1,"type":"result","command":"clean","action":"removed","path":"/tmp/rfm/symlink","detail":"symlink"}' ]
    [ "${lines[4]}" = '{"v":1,"type":"result","command":"clean","action":"removed","path":"/tmp/rfm/unmeasured","detail":""}' ]
    [ "${lines[5]}" = '{"v":1,"type":"result","command":"clean","action":"removed","path":"/tmp/rfm/text","detail":"12KB"}' ]
    [ "${lines[6]}" = '{"v":1,"type":"result","command":"clean","action":"skipped","path":"/tmp/rfm/skipped","detail":"protected"}' ]
    [ "${lines[7]}" = '{"v":1,"type":"result","command":"clean","action":"failed","path":"/tmp/rfm/failed","detail":"permission denied"}' ]
}

@test "one measurement serves the operations log and the event stream" {
    command -v jq > /dev/null || skip "jq is required"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2016  # the fake du expands these when it runs
    mole_test_fake_command du 'printf "%s\n" "$*" >> "$HOME/du-calls"; exec /usr/bin/du "$@"'
    : > "$HOME/du-calls"
    local name
    for name in neither log-only log-and-events events-only precomputed; do
        make_dir_with_blob "$HOME/data/$name" 64
    done

    run_safe_remove "$HOME/data/neither" MO_NO_OPLOG=1
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    run_safe_remove "$HOME/data/log-only"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    run_safe_remove "$HOME/data/log-and-events" MOLE_JSON_EVENTS_FILE="$EVENTS"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    run_safe_remove "$HOME/data/events-only" MO_NO_OPLOG=1 MOLE_JSON_EVENTS_FILE="$EVENTS"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    run_safe_remove "$HOME/data/precomputed" MO_NO_OPLOG=1 MOLE_JSON_EVENTS_FILE="$EVENTS" PRECOMPUTED_KB=4096
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]

    # Without the events file nothing changes: the operations log costs one du
    # and no log costs none. The event stream reuses that one du, measures
    # once when the log is off, and trusts a size the caller already measured.
    local neither log_only both events_only precomputed
    neither=$(count_du_calls "$HOME/data/neither")
    log_only=$(count_du_calls "$HOME/data/log-only")
    both=$(count_du_calls "$HOME/data/log-and-events")
    events_only=$(count_du_calls "$HOME/data/events-only")
    precomputed=$(count_du_calls "$HOME/data/precomputed")
    [ "$log_only" -eq $((neither + 1)) ]
    [ "$both" -eq "$log_only" ]
    [ "$events_only" -eq "$log_only" ]
    [ "$precomputed" -eq "$neither" ]

    run removed_size_of "$HOME/data/log-and-events"
    [ "$output" -ge 64 ]
    run removed_size_of "$HOME/data/events-only"
    [ "$output" -ge 64 ]
    run removed_size_of "$HOME/data/precomputed"
    [ "$output" = "4096" ]
}

@test "an empty file reports size_kb 0" {
    command -v jq > /dev/null || skip "jq is required"
    mkdir -p "$HOME/data"
    : > "$HOME/data/empty.bin"

    run_safe_remove "$HOME/data/empty.bin" MOLE_JSON_EVENTS_FILE="$EVENTS"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ ! -e "$HOME/data/empty.bin" ]
    run jq -r 'select(.type == "result") | [.action, .size_kb, .detail] | @tsv' "$EVENTS"
    [ "$output" = $'removed\t0\t' ]
}

@test "a size probe that fails leaves size_kb out" {
    command -v jq > /dev/null || skip "jq is required"
    # du prints a partial total and then fails, as it does on an unreadable child.
    mole_test_fake_command du 'echo 4; exit 1'
    make_dir_with_blob "$HOME/data/unmeasurable" 64

    run_safe_remove "$HOME/data/unmeasurable" MOLE_JSON_EVENTS_FILE="$EVENTS"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ ! -e "$HOME/data/unmeasurable" ]
    run jq -r 'select(.type == "result") | [.action, has("size_kb")] | @tsv' "$EVENTS"
    [ "$output" = $'removed\tfalse' ]
}

@test "a size probe that times out leaves size_kb out" {
    command -v jq > /dev/null || skip "jq is required"
    mole_test_fake_command du 'exec sleep 10'
    make_dir_with_blob "$HOME/data/slow" 64

    run_safe_remove "$HOME/data/slow" MOLE_JSON_EVENTS_FILE="$EVENTS" MOLE_TIMEOUT_DISK_VERIFY_SEC=2
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ ! -e "$HOME/data/slow" ]
    run jq -r 'select(.type == "result") | [.action, has("size_kb")] | @tsv' "$EVENTS"
    [ "$output" = $'removed\tfalse' ]
}

@test "safe_sudo_remove reports the size it measured" {
    command -v jq > /dev/null || skip "jq is required"
    make_dir_with_blob "$HOME/admin-cache/blobs" 64

    run env HOME="$HOME" PROJECT_ROOT="$PROJECT_ROOT" TARGET_DIR="$HOME/admin-cache/blobs" \
        MOLE_JSON_EVENTS_FILE="$EVENTS" MOLE_TEST_MODE=0 MOLE_TEST_NO_AUTH=0 \
        /bin/bash --noprofile --norc << 'EOF'
set -euo pipefail
source "$PROJECT_ROOT/lib/core/common.sh"
# Model a root-owned path, so safe_sudo_remove measures and removes the
# target itself, with a sudo that runs each command as this user.
_mole_privileged_path_has_mutable_ancestor() { return 1; }
sudo() {
    printf '%s\n' "$*" >> "$HOME/sudo-calls"
    [[ "${1:-}" == "-n" ]] || return 99
    shift
    "$@"
}
safe_sudo_remove "$TARGET_DIR"
EOF
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ ! -e "$HOME/admin-cache/blobs" ]
    run grep -c '^-n du -skP ' "$HOME/sudo-calls"
    [ "$output" -eq 1 ]
    run removed_size_of "$HOME/admin-cache/blobs"
    [ "$output" -ge 64 ]
}

@test "a selected run reports the size measured after the cache grew" {
    command -v jq > /dev/null || skip "jq is required"
    local alpha="$HOME/Library/Caches/com.example.alpha"
    # Four caches, so the section sizes them in parallel before removing any.
    make_cache com.example.alpha 256
    make_cache com.example.beta 64
    make_cache com.example.gamma 64
    make_cache com.example.delta 64
    set_mock_host_toolchains
    install_rm_guard

    run_clean_json --dry-run
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    local preview_kb
    preview_kb=$(jq -r --arg p "$alpha" 'select(.type == "item" and .path == $p) | .size_kb' "$EVENTS")
    [ "$preview_kb" -ge 256 ]

    dd if=/dev/zero of="$alpha/grown.bin" bs=1024 count=512 2> /dev/null
    local grown_kb
    grown_kb=$(du -skP "$alpha" | awk '{print $1}')
    [ "$grown_kb" -gt "$preview_kb" ]

    SELECTION_FILE="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/selection"
    printf '%s\0' "$alpha" > "$SELECTION_FILE"
    : > "$EVENTS"
    run_clean_json
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ ! -e "$alpha" ]
    [ -f "$HOME/Library/Caches/com.example.beta/blob.bin" ]

    run removed_size_of "$alpha"
    [ "${#lines[@]}" -eq 1 ]
    [ "$output" -ge "$grown_kb" ]
    [ ! -s "$RM_GUARD_LOG" ]
}

@test "MO_NO_OPLOG=1 still reports removed sizes in a selected run" {
    command -v jq > /dev/null || skip "jq is required"
    local alpha="$HOME/Library/Caches/com.example.alpha"
    make_cache com.example.alpha 128
    set_mock_host_toolchains
    install_rm_guard
    SELECTION_FILE="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/selection"
    printf '%s\0' "$alpha" > "$SELECTION_FILE"
    NO_OPLOG=1

    run_clean_json
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ ! -e "$alpha" ]
    # The operations log really was off.
    [ ! -e "$HOME/Library/Logs/mole/operations.log" ]
    run removed_size_of "$alpha"
    [ "$output" -ge 128 ]
    [ ! -s "$RM_GUARD_LOG" ]
}

@test "skipped and failed results never carry size_kb" {
    command -v jq > /dev/null || skip "jq is required"
    local caches="$HOME/Library/Caches"
    make_cache com.example.alpha 64
    make_cache com.example.beta 64
    # A read-only folder inside beta makes its removal fail part way.
    make_dir_with_blob "$caches/com.example.beta/locked" 16
    chmod 555 "$caches/com.example.beta/locked"
    set_mock_host_toolchains
    install_rm_guard
    SELECTION_FILE="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/selection"
    printf '%s\0' "$caches/com.example.alpha" "$caches/com.example.beta" > "$SELECTION_FILE"

    run_clean_json
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]

    # One result of each kind: alpha is removed, beta fails, and the engine's
    # own log folder is skipped as protected although nobody selected it.
    run removed_size_of "$caches/com.example.alpha"
    [ "$output" -ge 64 ]
    run jq -r --arg p "$caches/com.example.beta" 'select(.type == "result" and .path == $p) | .action' "$EVENTS"
    [ "$output" = "failed" ]
    run jq -r 'select(.type == "result" and .action == "skipped") | .path' "$EVENTS"
    [[ "$output" == *"$HOME/Library/Logs/mole"* ]] || return 1

    run jq -c 'select(.type == "result" and .action != "removed" and has("size_kb"))' "$EVENTS"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ -z "$output" ]
    [ ! -s "$RM_GUARD_LOG" ]
}

@test "a dry run writes no result events" {
    command -v jq > /dev/null || skip "jq is required"
    make_cache com.example.alpha 64
    set_mock_host_toolchains
    install_rm_guard

    run_clean_json --dry-run
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ -f "$HOME/Library/Caches/com.example.alpha/blob.bin" ]
    run jq -r 'select(.type == "item") | .path' "$EVENTS"
    [[ "$output" == *"$HOME/Library/Caches/com.example.alpha"* ]] || return 1
    run jq -c 'select(.type == "result")' "$EVENTS"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ -z "$output" ]
}
```

- [x] **Step 3: Run the tests to verify they fail**

Run: `scripts/mole-patches.sh test tests/clean_removed_sizes.bats`

Expected: `10 tests, 7 failures`. These fail because nothing carries a size yet:
- `result events carry size_kb only on removed results with a measured size`: `lines[0]` has no `"size_kb":1024`.
- `one measurement serves the operations log and the event stream`: `[ "$events_only" -eq "$log_only" ]` fails, because with the log off nothing is measured yet.
- `an empty file reports size_kb 0`: the output is `removed`, then two tabs, with no `0` between them.
- `safe_sudo_remove reports the size it measured`, `a selected run reports the size measured after the cache grew`, `MO_NO_OPLOG=1 still reports removed sizes in a selected run` and `skipped and failed results never carry size_kb`: `removed_size_of` prints `null`, so `[ "$output" -ge … ]` fails with "integer expression expected".

These already pass and must keep passing: `a size probe that fails leaves size_kb out`, `a size probe that times out leaves size_kb out` and `a dry run writes no result events`. They catch an implementation that reports `0` for an unmeasured item, or that writes results during a dry run.

- [x] **Step 4: Carry the size on removed results** — `lib/core/host.sh`

Find:
```bash
# Mirror of log_operation: one outcome for one path. Dry runs only preview,
# so they never report outcomes.
# Args: command, action (REMOVED/SKIPPED/FAILED), path, detail
mole_json_event_result() {
    mole_json_events_enabled || return 0
    if [[ "${MOLE_DRY_RUN:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        return 0
    fi
    local action=""
    case "${2-}" in
        REMOVED) action="removed" ;;
        SKIPPED) action="skipped" ;;
        FAILED) action="failed" ;;
        *) return 0 ;;
    esac
    mole_json_emit "{\"v\":1,\"type\":\"result\",\"command\":$(mole_json_str "${1-}"),\"action\":\"$action\",\"path\":$(mole_json_str "${3-}"),\"detail\":$(mole_json_str "${4-}")}"
}
```
Replace with:
```bash
# Mirror of log_operation: one outcome for one path. Dry runs only preview,
# so they never report outcomes.
# Args: command, action (REMOVED/SKIPPED/FAILED), path, detail, [size_kb]
# size_kb is the KiB a removal measured just before deleting the path. Only
# removed results carry it, and only when it is a whole number: an empty or
# other value means nothing was measured, and the key is left out, so a host
# can tell an empty item (0) from an unmeasured one.
mole_json_event_result() {
    mole_json_events_enabled || return 0
    if [[ "${MOLE_DRY_RUN:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        return 0
    fi
    local action=""
    case "${2-}" in
        REMOVED) action="removed" ;;
        SKIPPED) action="skipped" ;;
        FAILED) action="failed" ;;
        *) return 0 ;;
    esac
    local size_field=""
    if [[ "$action" == "removed" && "${5-}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        size_field=",\"size_kb\":$(mole_json_num "$5")"
    fi
    mole_json_emit "{\"v\":1,\"type\":\"result\",\"command\":$(mole_json_str "${1-}"),\"action\":\"$action\",\"path\":$(mole_json_str "${3-}"),\"detail\":$(mole_json_str "${4-}")$size_field}"
}
```

Replace with:
```markdown
  preview file, or Mole's test mode (`MOLE_TEST_MODE=1`), for example.

### Clean results (patch 0006)

- **`size_kb` on `removed` results.** A `removed` result carries `size_kb`: the KiB the
  engine measured for that path just before deleting it, measured the same way as the
  path's preview `size_kb`. `0` is a real size (an empty file or folder). The key is
  absent when the removal could not measure the path (its size probe failed or ran out
  of time). `skipped` and `failed` results never carry it, and dry runs still write no
  `result` events. Hosts charge `size_kb` when it is present and the preview size when
  it is absent.
- The size is measured whenever `MOLE_JSON_EVENTS_FILE` is set, even with `MO_NO_OPLOG=1`.
  With the operations log on, the log line and the event share one measurement, and a
  size the calling section already measured is reused without measuring again.
- Most clean items reach the removal with a size their section measured just before
  (`safe_clean` sizes its batch first). When that measurement fails the section passes
  `0`, so the result reads `size_kb: 0`. A preview whose own measurement failed the same
  way shows the row as `size_kb: 0` with `size_known: true`.
- Removals that do not go through `safe_remove` or `safe_sudo_remove` carry no `size_kb`:
  symlinks (`detail: "symlink"`), simulators (`"simulator"`), empty app containers
  (`"stub-container"`), the System section's batched and memory-report removals, and
  Time Machine.
- **`detail` on `removed` results is text for people.** It is the measured size in
  decimal units (Mole's `bytes_to_human`: 1 KB = 1000 bytes, as in `"922KB"` or
  `"3.1MB"`), empty for a zero-size item, or a word such as `"symlink"`. Never parse it;
  use `size_kb`. With the events file set it is filled in even with `MO_NO_OPLOG=1`.
- **`skipped` results also arrive for paths the host did not select.** Sections report
  protected paths they meet before the selection check (`detail: "protected"`; for
  example the engine's own `~/Library/Logs/mole`). Hosts ignore results for paths they
  did not select.

## Selections (`MOLE_SELECTION_FILE`, patch 0003)
```
